name: healthy Win11 server candidate with a battery (the peer's measured power shape)
note: Hand-built fixture for the Win11 side of the four-quadrant matrix. It carries exactly the values measured on the Win11 peer on 2026-09-23 (STANDBYIDLE DC = 0x00000e10 = 3600 s, S0 low-power-idle present) plus a configured serve listener and a patched trustedHosts, i.e. the 'everything is set up, only the power policy is a hazard' case. Host names and tailnet names are placeholders (never real ones). Expected under -Role server: 19 pass / 2 degraded / 0 blocked / 0 unknown (21 items) => exit 1, which is also how the degraded step of the exit-code ladder is proven. t49: the native group carries route_print4 (the tailnet destination spelled as the approved CIDR) so TAILNET_ROUTE_PRESENT answers instead of staying unknown, and the registry group's internet_settings lets SERVER_PROXY_STATE answer too - before t49 this fixture was 19 items with 17 pass. Sanitized round 2 2026-09-24 17:33 (t14): the remaining RFC1918 addresses were moved into neutral private ranges (10.20.0.0/16 for the LAN interface, plus the 10.21 and 10.22 host entries; the /16 membership is left readable) and the Tailscale IPv6 node suffix was replaced with the ::1000:1 (local) / ::1000:2 (peer) placeholder; the Tailscale IPv6 /48 product prefix is unchanged. Re-verify with: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File dsh-crossnet-link/tests/run-fixtures.ps1 Re-verify with: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File dsh-crossnet-link/tests/run-fixtures.ps1 Sanitized 2026-09-24 17:29 (t13): real captured identifiers were replaced with neutral placeholders (tailnet 100.64.0.11 local / 100.64.0.12 peer, non-tailnet 198.51.100.11, user paths C:/Users/<USER>); structure, indentation and field names are unchanged. Re-verify with: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File dsh-crossnet-link/tests/run-fixtures.ps1

    openBrowser: false
    trustedHosts: []

    trustedHosts:
      - server-example.tailXXXX.ts.net
